root_cause: The dropdown's keydown handler unconditionally calls event.stopPropagation() for the Escape key, preventing the event from bubbling up to the modal's escape handler when the dropdown menu is closed. This prevents the modal from closing when pressing Escape on the access toggle button.
repair_strategy: Modify the dropdown's dataApiKeydownHandler to only stopPropagation for Escape when the dropdown menu is open (isActive). When the dropdown is closed, allow the Escape event to propagate so the modal can handle it and close.
expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Escape while focused on the access toggle button will now close the share dialog (modal) and return focus to the Share button, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard). When the dropdown menu is open, pressing Escape will close only the dropdown and return focus to the toggle button, preserving the existing behavior.
functional_risks: If a dropdown is used outside a modal, the Escape key will no longer be stopped when the dropdown is closed, which could cause unexpected behavior if there are other Escape handlers on ancestors. However, the dropdown only stops propagation for Escape when open, which is the standard pattern.
Other keys (ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Space) remain unchanged.
verification_requirements: Pressing Escape with focus on the access toggle button (dropdown closed) closes the share dialog and returns focus to the Share button.
Pressing Escape with focus on a dropdown menu item (dropdown open) closes the dropdown and returns focus to the toggle button, modal remains open.
ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Space, and Enter keyboard navigation inside the dropdown continues to work as expected.
Modal keyboard escape handling remains functional for other focus positions inside the modal.
